title: Section cores over a point or interval identify the flat sharp mapping test
statement:
Use small quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, equivalence edges and cores from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], marked products and flat and sharp markings from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], and categorical equivalences from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $B=\Delta^0$ or $B=\Delta^1$, let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration between quasicategories, and mark $E$ by precisely those edges that lie in a vertex fibre $E_b=E\times_B\{b\}$ and are equivalences in that fibre; denote this marked set by $E^{\mathrm{v}\simeq}$. Define the strict section simplicial set by
$$\operatorname{Sec}_B(E)=\operatorname{Fun}(B,E)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,B)}\{\mathrm{id}_B\}.$$
Its $n$-simplices are maps $B\times\Delta^n\to E$ whose composite with $p$ is the projection to $B$. Then $\operatorname{Sec}_B(E)$ is a quasicategory, and there is a natural identity of simplicial sets
$$\operatorname{Sec}_B(E)^\simeq=\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_B(B^\flat,E^{\mathrm{v}\simeq}),\qquad \operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_B(B^\flat,E^{\mathrm{v}\simeq})_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{/B^\flat}(B^\flat\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,E^{\mathrm{v}\simeq}).$$
If $q:F\to B$ is another such inner fibration and $u:E\to F$ is a categorical equivalence with $qu=p$, postcomposition induces a categorical equivalence $\operatorname{Sec}_B(E)\to\operatorname{Sec}_B(F)$ and a weak homotopy equivalence on their cores. These assertions permit empty fibres and empty section quasicategories; no quasi-inverse over $B$ is required.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Lemma B.2.4(c), printed p.1484: section-core justification of the point and interval tests; explicit strict-fibre refinement of the proof. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical fact.

proof.text: An equivalence in $B=\Delta^0$ or $\Delta^1$ is an identity: an inverse would give inequalities in both directions between its endpoints, so the endpoints coincide and the unique edge is degenerate. Hence $p:E\to B$ is an isofibration as defined in [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]: its inner lifting property is assumed, and the identity at $p(x)$ lifts to the identity at $x$. Apply that node with $\varnothing\hookrightarrow B$. It gives an isofibration $p_*:\operatorname{Fun}(B,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,B)$ between quasicategories. The strict fibre at $\mathrm{id}_B$ is a quasicategory: an inner horn in the fibre is a lifting problem for $p_*$ with bottom the constant simplex at $\mathrm{id}_B$, so its lift remains in the fibre. This fibre is exactly $\operatorname{Sec}_B(E)$, by the degreewise pullback and functor definitions. The same argument applies to $F$.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4(c), printed p.1484; agent-written expansion of the strict-section argument. Archival source WANTED.

proof.text: The section fibre is the full simplicial subset of $\operatorname{Fun}(B,E)$ on its section vertices. Indeed, if $h:B\times\Delta^n\to E$ has section vertices, $ph$ and the projection have the same value $b$ at every product vertex $(b,i)$. A simplex of $\Delta^0$ or $\Delta^1$ is uniquely determined by its ordered vertices (it is a weakly increasing map to $[0]$ or $[1]$). Applying this to every simplex of the product gives $ph=\operatorname{pr}_B$. For an edge between section vertices, equivalence in this full subset is therefore equivalent to equivalence in the ambient functor quasicategory: the inverse edge and its two inverse triangles have only those vertices and hence remain in the full subset. Conversely an inverse there is an inverse in the ambient category.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4(c), printed p.1484; agent-written expansion of the strict-section argument. Archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Let $\tau$ be an edge of $\operatorname{Sec}_B(E)$. By Step 2 and [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences], $\tau$ is an equivalence precisely when its component at each vertex $b$ is an equivalence in $E$. These components lie in $E_b$. For any edge $a$ of $E_b$, equivalence in $E_b$ implies equivalence in $E$ by inclusion. Conversely, an inverse in $E$ for such an $a$ has both endpoints over $b$. Its image in $B$ is the unique edge from $b$ to $b$, hence is degenerate; both inverse triangles project to the constant triangle at $b$, since all their vertices do. Thus the inverse witnesses lie in $E_b$. Therefore the section equivalences are exactly the transformations whose components are equivalences in their vertex fibres.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4(c), printed p.1484; agent-written expansion of the strict-section argument. Archival source WANTED.

proof.text: In the coordinatewise product marking of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], the marked edges of $B^\flat\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp$ are exactly the pairs $(s_0b,\alpha)$, where $b$ is a vertex of $B$ and $\alpha$ is any edge of $\Delta^n$. Consequently an underlying section family $h:B\times\Delta^n\to E$ is a marked map to $E^{\mathrm{v}\simeq}$ if and only if every component $h(b,\alpha)$ is an equivalence in $E_b$. By Step 3 this is equivalent to every edge of the corresponding $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{Sec}_B(E)$ being an equivalence. This is precisely membership in its core, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Both sides are thus the very same subset of the same families in every degree, not merely equivalent spaces. Their simplicial operators both precompose on $\Delta^n$, so these degreewise identities give the asserted identity of simplicial sets.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4(c), printed p.1484; agent-written expansion of the strict-section argument. Archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Now assume $qu=p$ and $u$ is a categorical equivalence. By [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations](2), choose an ordinary simplicial quasi-inverse $v:F\to E$ and inverse natural equivalences $vu\simeq\mathrm{id}_E$, $uv\simeq\mathrm{id}_F$. Postcomposition $u_*:\operatorname{Fun}(B,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,F)$ has quasi-inverse $v_*$. For example the evaluation formula $(h,t)\mapsto\eta(h(-),t)$ for an inverse transformation $\eta$ defines the transformation $v_*u_*\to\mathrm{id}$. It is an equivalence: at every vertex $h$ its component is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(B,E)$ by the pointwise criterion applied at the vertices of $B$; the same criterion applied with domain $\operatorname{Fun}(B,E)$ proves the assertion for the transformation itself. The other inverse transformation is treated identically. Hence $u_*$ is a functor equivalence, and it is strictly over $\operatorname{Fun}(B,B)$ because $qu=p$. No assertion that $v$ is over $B$ has been used.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4(c), printed p.1484; agent-written expansion of the strict-section argument. Archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Step 1 gives isofibrations $p_*$ and $q_*$ over the common quasicategory $\operatorname{Fun}(B,B)$; Step 5 gives the functor equivalence $u_*$ commuting with these projections. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-base-change] with $\mathcal R=\Delta^0$ and $h$ the vertex $\mathrm{id}_B$. Its strict pullbacks are exactly the two section quasicategories, and its induced equivalence is exactly postcomposition by $u$ on their defining families. By [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations](2) this functor equivalence is a categorical equivalence. The general final clause of [lem-coef-quasicategory-full-subcategory-core-equivalence] then gives a weak homotopy equivalence on their cores. This uses the general clause for every functor equivalence, not the narrower clause about replete full subcategories.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4(c), printed p.1484; agent-written expansion of the strict-section argument. Archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Naturality follows directly from the identity of families in Step 4: a map over $B$ sends a fibre edge and its inverse triangles into the corresponding fibre, hence preserves $E^{\mathrm{v}\simeq}$ and commutes with the degreewise identification by postcomposition. Pulling a family back along a map between the allowed point and interval bases also commutes with it by precomposition. No step chooses a vertex in any fibre or section category. If a fibre is empty there is no section since $B$ is nonempty, and both displayed section-core and marked-map simplicial sets are empty. If all fibres are nonempty but there are no sections (for example, $E$ is the discrete two-point simplicial set mapping to the two different vertices of $\Delta^1$), both sets are again empty. The isofibration base-change theorem and the general core-equivalence clause permit empty quasicategories, so the equivalence assertion covers these cases too.
